project: Chat Run Scoping and Source Navigation Parity (0009d)
overview: Implement parity v1 chat run scoping (L1), source-to-evidence navigation, mismatch warnings, and onboarding/disabled states without expanding to L2/L3 complexity.
goals: Ship active run chip and recent completed run picker in chat.
Extend chat API to return selected/effective run metadata and mismatch signal.
Enable source chips to jump to evidence when anchors are available.
nonGoals: L2 strict isolation and L3 multi-run compare behavior.
Large backend retrieval orchestration changes outside optional run_id scope.
successMetrics: Operators can explicitly choose run context for chat.
Mismatch between selected and effective run is always visible.
Source jump success/fallback behavior is deterministic and user-visible.
openQuestions: Should chat sources be persisted as citation rows (`chat_message` + citations) or emitted as ephemeral anchors in parity v1?

resolvedDecisions.decision: Use soft fallback with mandatory mismatch disclosure for run-scoped chat L1.
details: When no completed runs exist, `effective_run_id` is null and `effective_index_version` is disclosed.
Fallback never occurs silently; mismatch UI is required.

resolvedDecisions.decision: Use strict anchor-only source jumps in parity v1.
details: Source jumps are enabled only when `anchor_state=ready`.
Default clickable emphasis is gated by measured anchor coverage >= 80%.

routes.name: Evidence Viewer
routes.purpose: Jump target for chat source chips when anchor exists.

uiNotes: Keep L1 behavior explicit in labels and warnings.
Disabled source chips require friendly explanation copy.
Suggested prompts are insert-only, never auto-send.
rules: Scope lock is L1 only for parity v1.
Run-scope fallback must always disclose mismatch via explicit metadata and reason code.
Default source-jump emphasis is gated by measured anchor coverage >= 80%.
No-context states must disable input with recovery guidance.

stories.title: Add active run chip and picker to chat
stories.description: As an operator, I want run selection controls in chat so I can choose context intentionally.
acceptanceCriteria: Chat renders active run chip and a selector seeded from recent completed runs.
Example: selecting run R123 updates chip and outbound request payload to include run_id=R123.
Negative: unknown/incompatible runs are not presented as normal selectable options.

stories.title: Extend chat API with run scope metadata
stories.description: As an operator, I want selected/effective run metadata in chat responses so scope behavior is transparent.
acceptanceCriteria: `POST /api/folders/:id/chat` accepts optional run_id and emits selected/effective/mismatch metadata with `scope_reason`.
Example: stale selected run produces mismatch=true, deterministic `scope_reason`, and disclosed effective_run_id fallback.
Negative: invalid run_id must not be ignored without explicit mismatch signal and reason.

stories.title: Enable source-chip jump to evidence with fallback
stories.description: As an operator, I want source chips to open evidence directly when possible and fail gracefully when not.
acceptanceCriteria: Source chips with `anchor_state=ready` navigate to evidence viewer target.
Example: clicking a source opens the corresponding citation target in viewer.
Negative: source chips without ready anchors are disabled with explanatory copy and do not navigate.

stories.title: Add selected-message sources rail and mismatch warning
stories.description: As an operator, I want message-specific source rail and mismatch warning UI so provenance and scope are easy to inspect.
acceptanceCriteria: Selecting a response message updates a side rail with sources for that message only.
Example: mismatch warning shows selected and effective run IDs inline in chat.
Negative: rail content must not remain stale after changing selected message.

stories.title: Ship empty and no-context chat onboarding
stories.description: As an operator, I want onboarding prompts and disabled-input guidance when context is missing.
acceptanceCriteria: Empty state includes suggested prompts that inject into composer without auto-send.
Example: no indexed docs disables composer and points user to setup action.
Negative: input cannot be silently disabled with no guidance text.
